key_insight: The paper shows that the performance gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous optimization cannot be closed by common similarity or weak interpolation assumptions, and that only a stronger combined assumption set yields a better time-complexity guarantee.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this means reduced-worker-synchronization assumptions alone are not enough to justify homogeneous-like speedups on non-identical data, so algorithm design must account explicitly for heterogeneity.
method: Prove impossibility results under first- and second-order similarity assumptions for any randomized algorithm.
Show that weak interpolation alone still cannot remove the heterogeneous time-complexity gap.
Derive a new bound using strong interpolation plus the local Polyak-Lojasiewicz condition, matching the best homogeneous worker-time dependence.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical time-complexity analysis and impossibility/proof results rather than experimental evaluation.
watch_item: The improved bound depends on stronger assumptions that may be difficult to verify or satisfy in real heterogeneous training pipelines.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
